1.name: In which weather do ingredient combining and breaking down always succeed?
1.note: In Strong Wind and Hurricane, combining and breaking down succeed 100% of the time.

2.name: In which weather do Market ingredients get cheaper?

3.name: During business, which weather gives the biggest EXP bonus?

4.name: On a Blood Moon night, what are you most likely to see more of in your restaurant?
4.note: During a Blood Moon, the chance of a roach at each table doubles.

5.name: Which of these is not a recipe taste?
5.note: The six recipe tastes are Sour, Sweet, Bitter, Spicy, Salty and Umami.

6.name: Which recipe grade is the highest?

7.name: What's the main reason to sear meat before stewing it?
7.note: "Sealing in the juices" is a widespread myth: seared meat loses just as much liquid. It's mostly about flavor.

8.name: How should you add the oil when making mayonnaise?
8.note: Add the oil too fast and the mayo splits.
lines: A little at a time, whisking as you go
Heat it first, then pour it in

9.name: To whip egg whites so stiff you can turn the bowl upside down, what matters most?
9.note: The tiniest trace of grease or yolk will stop the whites from whipping up.
lines: Not a speck of grease in the bowl
You must use a copper bowl

10.name: Is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable?

11.name: What do you dip your fries in?

13.name: Which weather gives the most Seasonal points?

14.name: Which weather boosts cookware enhancement success the most?

15.name: Which weather lowers the picky rate the most?
15.note: Deep Freeze: picky rate -35%, Blood Moon -30%, Severe Thunderstorm -25%.

16.name: How much does it cost to remove a gem in Acid Rain?
16.note: In Acid Rain, removing gems is free.

17.name: When does cooking a signature dish get the biggest boost to the chance of a higher grade?

18.name: How many recipe tastes are there?
18.note: The six recipe tastes are Sour, Sweet, Bitter, Spicy, Salty and Umami.

19.name: When there's a Rainbow, what's the takeaway renown bonus?

20.name: In 2025, mathematician Wang Hong, a Peking University graduate, and her collaborator proved the 3D Kakeya conjecture. What question did the conjecture start from?
20.note: The other three are famous math problems too. Kakeya asked about turning a needle around: the answer is that the area can be as small as you like.
lines: The smallest area a needle must sweep to turn around in a plane
The fewest colors a map needs so neighboring countries always differ
The most space-saving way to stack oranges
How many times a sheet of paper can be folded in half

21.name: What is the "Kakeya" in "Kakeya conjecture"?
21.note: Japanese mathematician Sōichi Kakeya posed the needle problem in 1917.
lines: The surname of a Japanese mathematician

22.name: Where did Wang Hong do her undergraduate degree?
22.note: Wang Hong studied at Peking University's School of Mathematical Sciences.

23.name: To color a map so that neighboring countries never share a color, what's the smallest number of colors that is always enough?
23.note: This is the famous Four Color Theorem.

24.name: When is "Pi Day"?
24.note: Pi starts with 3.14, so Pi Day is March 14 (3/14).

25.name: How many people does a class need before the chance that two share a birthday is over 50%?
25.note: Far fewer than you'd think, right? This is the famous Birthday Paradox.

26.name: A prize is behind one of three doors. You pick one, the host opens another, empty door and asks if you want to switch. What gives you a better chance?
26.note: Switching wins 2 times out of 3; staying wins only 1 time out of 3.

27.name: Boiling water for noodles high up a mountain, compared with at the bottom, what happens?
27.note: Air pressure is lower up high, so water boils before reaching 100°C, which makes noodles harder to cook through.
lines: It boils sooner, but isn't as hot

28.name: Your mouth is on fire from spicy food. What puts it out best?
28.note: Capsaicin doesn't dissolve in water, but the casein and fat in milk carry it away.

29.name: When an AI confidently makes up things that don't exist, what do people call it?

30.name: In "ChatGPT", what does the final T of "GPT" stand for?

31.name: In 2016, the Go AI AlphaGo beat which player?
31.note: The next year it also beat Ke Jie.

32.name: How many letter r's are in the English word strawberry?
32.note: This one used to trip up a lot of AIs.

33.name: What do AI-drawn people most often get mocked for getting wrong?
33.note: AI often draws hands with six fingers, or even more.

34.name: What does the Turing test test?
lines: Whether a person chatting with a machine can tell it's a machine

35.name: An "overfitted" AI model is most like which kind of student?
35.note: Overfitting means learning the practice questions too rigidly, so new questions trip you up.
lines: One who memorized the practice questions and is lost if a number changes
One who always sleeps in class
One who always hands in the test early

36.name: What's the usual name for the instructions you type when talking to an AI?
36.note: What you write to tell an AI what you want is called a prompt.

37.name: The meme of a dog holding a mug in a burning room, saying "This is fine", is usually used to mean?
lines: Pretending everything's normal when it clearly isn't
The room is nice and warm

38.name: The meme dog with its head tilted, surrounded by weird captions: what breed is it?
38.note: The meme is called Doge, and the original dog was a Japanese Shiba Inu named Kabosu.

39.name: What is "Big Ben" actually the name of?
39.note: The tower is the Elizabeth Tower; Big Ben is the biggest bell inside it.
lines: The great bell in the clock tower
The man who fixes the clock

40.name: What does the famous "Mind the gap" announcement on the London Underground warn passengers about?
40.note: It's a reminder not to step into the space between the train and the platform.
lines: The gap between the train and the platform

41.name: Traditional fish and chips used to be sold wrapped in what?
41.note: They used to come wrapped in old newspaper, until hygiene rules put a stop to it.

42.name: What is the "black pudding" in a full English breakfast mainly made of?
42.note: Black pudding is a blood sausage made with pork blood, fat and oats.

43.name: There's a spread people either adore or can't stand, and even its ads say so. What is it?
43.note: It's Marmite, and its slogan is literally "Love it or hate it".

44.name: What's the classic color of a double-decker bus?
44.note: The red double-decker bus is one of London's best-known symbols.

45.name: Tea with milk: milk in first, or tea first?

46.name: Scones: cream first, or jam first?

48.name: Zongzi (sticky rice dumplings): sweet or savory?

51.name: Fried eggs: well done or runny?

52.name: Cilantro: love it or hate it?

53.name: Hot pot: meat in first, or veggies first?

55.name: Which weather adds the most coins per table?
55.note: Deep Freeze: coins per table +10, Heavy Snow and Blizzard +1.

56.name: Which weather cuts occupancy by 35% but gives +60% final coins and final EXP?
56.note: Smog: occupancy -35%, final coins and final EXP +60% each.

57.name: In which weather do Market prices go up the most?
57.note: Acid Rain: Market prices +300%, Deep Freeze +250%, Blizzard +200%.

58.name: Which weather makes mystery recipe appraisal more likely to succeed?
58.note: Starry Night: mystery recipe appraisal success +5%.

59.name: In which weather can you swap friends' locked ingredients?
59.note: In a Hurricane you can swap friends' locked ingredients, at double the fee.

60.name: Which weather boosts missile critical rate the most?
60.note: Starry Night: missile critical rate +15%, Severe Thunderstorm +8%, Thunderstorm +5%.

61.name: The Kakeya conjecture proved by Wang Hong and her collaborator is about space in how many dimensions?
61.note: The 2D case was settled long ago; 3D was the real sticking point.

62.name: Which Chinese-heritage mathematician is often called "the Mozart of Math"?
62.note: Terence Tao became a full professor at 24 and won the Fields Medal at 31.

63.name: How many hearts does an octopus have?
63.note: Two pump blood to the gills, and one to the rest of the body.

64.name: How many neck vertebrae does a giraffe have?
64.note: Each of a giraffe's neck vertebrae is extra long.

65.name: Do snails have teeth?
65.note: A snail's tongue is covered in rows of tiny teeth, which can number over ten thousand.
lines: Yes, over ten thousand of them

66.name: Roughly how many bones does an adult human have?
66.note: Babies have more bones; some fuse together as they grow, leaving 206.

67.name: How many seconds are there in a day?

68.name: What happens to a sealed jar of honey left for many years?
68.note: Honey is very sweet and low in water, so bacteria can barely survive in it.
lines: It goes bad within a month

69.name: You put an egg in a bowl of water and it sinks to the bottom. What does that tell you?
69.note: As an egg ages, the air pocket inside grows, so older eggs float more easily.

70.name: Why do bananas ripen faster when kept next to apples?
70.note: Apples give off ethylene, a gas that makes fruit ripen faster.
lines: Apples give off a ripening gas

71.name: Which of these actually helps stop tears when you chop onions?
71.note: A cold onion releases less of the irritating gas, so it stings your eyes less.
lines: Chill the onion in the fridge first

72.name: In a thunderstorm, why do you always see the lightning before you hear the thunder?
72.note: Light travels about 300,000 km a second; sound only about 340 meters.
lines: Thunder takes the long way round

73.name: Who came up with the "Three Laws of Robotics"?
73.note: Isaac Asimov set out the Three Laws in a 1942 short story.

74.name: Which movie does the robot who says "I'll be back" come from?
74.note: It's Arnold Schwarzenegger's line in The Terminator.

75.name: Using AI to put one person's face onto someone else in a video is usually called?

76.name: What usually happens when you tell an AI to "think it through step by step" before answering?
76.note: This is called "chain of thought": writing out the steps in between makes mistakes less likely.

77.name: How does an AI read a piece of text?
77.note: These chunks are called tokens. One can be a word, part of a word, or a punctuation mark.
lines: It cuts the text into small chunks
It turns it into math formulas first
It looks at the shapes of the letters

78.name: What do you call the thing on your phone that listens to you and sets alarms for you?
78.note: Siri on your phone is one example of a voice assistant.

79.name: What is a "Rickroll"?
79.note: The song is Rick Astley's 1987 breakout hit.
lines: Clicking a link that turns out to play an '80s music video

80.name: The picture of a man turning to look at a passer-by while his girlfriend glares at him is usually used to mean?
80.note: This meme is known as "Distracted Boyfriend".
lines: Being tempted away by something new

81.name: Where does the phrase "Keep Calm and Carry On" come from?
81.note: The poster was printed in 1939, but almost none were ever put up.
lines: A British propaganda poster from World War II

82.name: What do people call the internet cat that always looks annoyed?
82.note: Grumpy Cat was born with that face, but was actually very easygoing.

83.name: What is the body of "Nyan Cat", the cat flying with a rainbow trail, made of?
83.note: Its body is a jam-filled toaster pastry with pink frosting.

84.name: In the "Stonks" meme, what word is deliberately misspelled?
84.note: "Stonks" misspells "stocks" on purpose, to poke fun at clueless investing.

85.name: How many pins does a British electrical plug have?
85.note: A British plug has three rectangular pins, and the longest is the earth pin.

86.name: Which side of the road do you drive on in the UK?
86.note: In the UK you drive on the left, with the steering wheel on the right.

87.name: What is the "London Eye"?
87.note: The London Eye opened in 2000, and one full turn takes about 30 minutes.
lines: A giant Ferris wheel on the Thames

88.name: In traditional Scottish dress, what's the tartan skirt worn by men called?
88.note: The kilt is the traditional dress of men from the Scottish Highlands.

89.name: A ring of huge standing stones, and nobody can say for sure how they got there. Which country is it in?
89.note: That's Stonehenge in England, some 4,000 to 5,000 years old.

90.name: A pinch of salt on watermelon?

91.name: Tomato and egg stir-fry: sugar or no sugar?

96.name: Soup before the meal or after?

97.name: Weekends: stay in or go out?
